A SUPPLY RUN with two interchangeable drop points, and the pairing only becomes visible in the raw wikitext. The rendered page flattens the Notes section into four unlabelled bullets; the source groups them under two zone sub-headings -- 'Beaucedine Glacier (S):' (Gate Sentry at F-6 near the Xarcabard zone line, stronghold at I-8, talk to Disserond, R.K.) and 'Xarcabard (S):' (Gate Sentry at J-9 near the Beaucedine zone line, stronghold at H-8, talk to Yimi Jomkeh, M.C.). So each branch is collect-and-deliver WITHIN one zone, and the two sentries sit on either side of the same zone line. The walkthrough itself names neither stronghold NPC -- both names come from that after-section, hence the flag.

OR BRANCH MODELLED AS GROUPS, on purpose. Bullet 2 says 'either', so this is a choice, not an unordered set; but each alternative has its own zone, so grouping them makes both draw and only the one for the zone the player is standing in can ever appear. The alternative -- one zone-less step named 'Gate Sentry' -- would match Gate Sentries in campaign zones that have nothing to do with this op. Group 'checkpoint' is the two sentries, group 'delivery' the two strongholds; a player does exactly one of each.

Bullet 3 is an OUTCOME of talking to the sentry, not a step: he hands you a package and lands Silence, Amnesia and Gravity on you (that is the difficulty of the op). The package is never named, so it cannot be evidence -- nothing here is observable.

notes:
THIRTEEN bullets, FOUR steps. Most of this walkthrough is an explanation of the crystal-matching minigame rather than instructions: bullet 4 describes the scene, bullet 7 is the three-menu key of worker appearance to element, bullets 9-11 are scoring behaviour (right element = crafting animation, wrong element = penalty and a menu delay, ignoring a worker costs less than answering wrong) and bullet 12 is the XP outcome with the figure unknown. Only bullets 1-3 (get the op, find the Fortification's arbiter), 5/6/8 (choose the element for a worker who has stopped moving) and 13 (report back) are things the player does.

ZONE IS NULL on steps 2 and 3: bullet 1 says 'a Northlands area that is under Windurst control', which rotates with front-line control, and no zone is ever named. The workers running in and out are described only by race and clothing, never named, so the minigame step has no target at all -- it is an unmarkable rung, kept because it is the substance of the op.

The header's Campaign Rank is a {{Question}} placeholder, so there is nothing to record from this page; the cached Category:Campaign Ops table gives 'Brass Wings of Service §' plus a 'Your Nation controls a Northlands Field' unlock, neither of which the schema can express and neither of which is a character level. 'Unit Requirement: 1 member.' is a party-size note with no field either. No Repeatable or Expansion field.
